ideas.a: It is released by a ductless gland straight into the bloodstream
It acts on a target organ somewhere else in the body
Many are proteins

model: A signal substance that a ductless gland releases into the bloodstream; it travels round the body and acts on a target organ elsewhere.

ideas.a: It has no duct
It secretes straight into the blood
It makes chemical messengers, e.g. the thyroid or pituitary

model: An organ with no duct that releases chemical messengers straight into the blood, such as the pituitary.

ideas.a: Its product leaves through a little tube
Examples: the sweat, tear or salivary glands
What it makes does not go into the blood

model: An organ that empties what it makes down a little tube, like the ones that make sweat or tears; its product does not go into the bloodstream.

ideas.a: It makes FSH, LH, TSH, ADH and oxytocin
It controls the other glands, such as the thyroid and ovaries
It hangs from the underside of the head's control centre, inside the skull

model: Sits deep in the head and bosses the thyroid and ovaries about: it makes TSH, FSH, LH, ADH and oxytocin.

ideas.a: It controls how fast cells respire and release energy
It controls growth and development in children
TSH from the pituitary makes the gland release it
It is made by a gland wrapped round the windpipe

model: Made by a gland around the windpipe when TSH arrives; it sets how fast cells respire and release energy, and controls growth in children.

ideas.a: It is made by the glands on top of the kidneys
It is released when you face danger or stress
It speeds up the heart rate and breathing

model: Made by the glands sitting on the kidneys when you face danger; it speeds up the heart rate and breathing so you can run away.

ideas.a: It is made by the islets of Langerhans
It makes cells take in the blood's fuel, and the liver store it as glycogen
Some people have to inject it

model: Made in the islets of Langerhans after a meal; it makes the liver store the extra fuel as glycogen. Some people have to inject it.

ideas.a: It is released by the pituitary
It makes the collecting ducts of the nephrons reabsorb more
It is released when you are dehydrated

model: Released by the pituitary when you are dehydrated; it makes the collecting ducts of the nephrons reabsorb more, so you keep your fluid.

ideas.a: It is made by the pituitary
It acts on the gland in the neck
Feedback switches it off when there is enough of the other hormone

model: Made by the pituitary; it travels to the gland in the neck and makes it release its hormone. Feedback switches it off when there is enough.

ideas.a: It is made by the pituitary
It makes the muscles of the uterus contract
It lets breastfeeding happen

model: Made by the pituitary; it makes the muscles of the uterus contract to push the baby out, and helps breastfeeding to start.

ideas.a: It is made by four tiny glands in the neck
It raises the level of a mineral in the blood
That mineral is what skeletons and teeth are made of

model: Made by four tiny glands at the back of the neck; it raises the level in the blood of the mineral that skeletons and teeth are made of.

ideas.a: It is made in the organs in the scrotum
It gives a beard, a deeper voice and more muscle at puberty
Anabolic steroids copy it

model: Made in the scrotum from puberty on; it gives a beard, a deeper voice and more muscle. Anabolic steroids copy it.

ideas.a: It is made by the developing Graafian follicle
It builds up the lining of the uterus after a period
It gives breasts and wider hips at puberty

model: Made by the developing Graafian follicle; it builds up the lining of the uterus again after a period, and widens the hips at puberty.

ideas.a: A change triggers a response that undoes it, back to normal
For example, high thyroxine switches off TSH
It keeps conditions steady

model: When a level drifts, the response pushes it back to normal and then switches itself off, keeping things steady: high thyroxine stops TSH.

ideas.a: Groups of cells in the gland behind the stomach
They make the hormone that lowers blood glucose
They are the endocrine part of a gland that also makes digestive enzymes

model: Little groups of cells in the gland behind the stomach; they release the hormone that lowers blood glucose after a meal.

ideas.a: Keeping conditions inside the body steady
For example temperature, water and blood glucose
Receptors, a control centre and effectors do it

model: Keeping conditions inside you steady, like body temperature and blood glucose, using receptors, a control centre and effectors.

ideas.a: They copy the male sex hormone
They are banned in sport as cheating
They build strength and bulk
They can damage the liver and heart

model: Drugs that copy the male sex hormone to build strength and bulk; banned in sport as cheating, and they can damage the liver and heart.
